programme.title: World's Most Incredible Hotels

programme.title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
programme.desc: Exploring the palaces of Saddam Hussein; discovering how he calls upon the ancient Egyptians and Babylonians for inspiration; how the architecture changes over time in response to threats from Iran and the United States.

programme.title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
programme.sub-title: Malkata Palace: Pharaoh, Foreigners, and Gods
programme.desc: Traveling back to the 14th century B.C. in Egypt; how the Malkata Palace represents a microcosm of Egypt; architectural details reveal insights about religious rituals and how pharaohs attempt to assert their domination over others.

programme.title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
programme.sub-title: Amarna: Palace of the First Sun King
programme.desc: Akhenaten shifts Egypt's capital to Amarna; how his worship of the sun disk defines an era built on temple crops, sacrifices and obedience to the pharaoh; how relocating his seat of power helps Akhenaten wrestle authority away from religious leaders.

programme.title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
programme.sub-title: Phaistos: Palaces Between Asia and Europe
programme.desc: Studying Bronze Age Crete; the myth of Daedalus and his labyrinth symbolizes Crete's location at the intersection of multiple cultures; discovering the Phaistos Palace, the site of extravagant religious rituals and entertainment spectacles.

programme.title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
programme.sub-title: Palace of Nestor at Pylos and Bronze Age Greece
programme.desc: Exploring the Palace of Nestor, a complex centered around the throne room; the ancient styles the Mycenaeans develop to bring these elaborate structures to life; what the arrangement of rooms reveals about how royals live and maintain control.

programme.title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
programme.sub-title: The Assyrian Palace at Nimrud: Empire in Stone
programme.desc: Ashurnasirpal II designs the Assyrian palace at Nimrud; he loves to write of his conquests of nature and his knowledge of tree species; clearly an intellectual, he describes in detail the glory of feasts he throws, as well as the math behind them.

programme.title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
programme.sub-title: Nineveh: The Architecture of Assyrian Power
programme.desc: Discovering the last great Assyrian palace and the largest city the world has ever seen before the Babylonian conquest; how its designers accomplish incredible civil engineering feats; meeting the lamassu guardians that flank the palace entrances.

programme.title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
programme.desc: The lore of Persepolis includes the exploits of many great kings; exploring the great citadel at Persepolis, with its famed flight of 111 steps leading to the Gate of All Nations; learning of its spectacular stone masonry and powerful art.

programme.title: Mr. Lincoln: The Life of Abraham Lincoln
programme.desc: Abraham Lincoln is born with little more than his natural talents; his father is more than contented with the life of a classic Jeffersonian farmer; the Lincolns move from Indiana to Illinois; Abraham strikes out on his own and never looks back.

programme.title: Mr. Lincoln: The Life of Abraham Lincoln
programme.desc: Lincoln's entry into politics coincides with the emergence of a new national political party, the Whigs; Lincoln at the forefront of Whig agitation to improve business; his own business ventures flop; he takes up law in Springfield, Illinois.

programme.title: Mr. Lincoln: The Life of Abraham Lincoln
programme.desc: Through his law partner, John Todd Stuart, Lincoln meets and marries Mary Todd in 1842; he wins the election to Congress in 1846, but his term is undistinguished; Lincoln returns to a life of domestic unhappiness; substantial success as an attorney.

programme.title: Mr. Lincoln: The Life of Abraham Lincoln
programme.desc: Lincoln's folksiness is a shield he rarely lets down; many see him as an introverted, slightly aloof lawyer; he dislikes wanna-be aristocrats and is a tremendous reader; he believes in God, but not the God of any formal religion.

programme.title: Mr. Lincoln: The Life of Abraham Lincoln
programme.desc: Lincoln expects that slavery will die out; instead, it experiences a revolution in profitability; in 1854, Stephen A. Douglas opens the western territories to slave expansion through the Kansas-Nebraska Act; Lincoln reenters politics in opposition.

programme.title: Mr. Lincoln: The Life of Abraham Lincoln
programme.desc: Lincoln challenges Douglas for the Illinois senate seat in 1858; Douglas portrays Lincoln as an abolitionist fanatic; Lincoln condemns Douglas's indifference to the moral wrong of slavery; Lincoln narrowly loses the election but gains attention.

programme.title: Mr. Lincoln: The Life of Abraham Lincoln
programme.desc: Lincoln impresses East Coast Republicans with an address at New York's Cooper Institute; his backers stage-manage his nomination at the Republican convention in May 1860; he wins the presidency by garnering almost all the North's electoral votes.

programme.title: Mr. Lincoln: The Life of Abraham Lincoln
programme.desc: South Carolina leads the Southern states in seceding from the Union; whether Lincoln has the skill to manage the situation; he responds to the South's attack on Ft. Sumter by calling out the militia; turning to George McClellan as his strategist.

programme.desc: Lincoln challenges Douglas for the Illinois senate seat in 1858; Douglas portrays Lincoln as an abolitionist fanatic; Lincoln condemns Douglas's indifference to the moral wrong of slavery; Lincoln narrowly loses the election but gains attention.

programme.title: Mr. Lincoln: The Life of Abraham Lincoln
programme.desc: Lincoln impresses East Coast Republicans with an address at New York's Cooper Institute; his backers stage-manage his nomination at the Republican convention in May 1860; he wins the presidency by garnering almost all the North's electoral votes.

programme.title: Mr. Lincoln: The Life of Abraham Lincoln
programme.desc: South Carolina leads the Southern states in seceding from the Union; whether Lincoln has the skill to manage the situation; he responds to the South's attack on Ft. Sumter by calling out the militia; turning to George McClellan as his strategist.

programme.title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
programme.desc: Exploring the palaces of Saddam Hussein; discovering how he calls upon the ancient Egyptians and Babylonians for inspiration; how the architecture changes over time in response to threats from Iran and the United States.

programme.title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
programme.sub-title: Malkata Palace: Pharaoh, Foreigners, and Gods
programme.desc: Traveling back to the 14th century B.C. in Egypt; how the Malkata Palace represents a microcosm of Egypt; architectural details reveal insights about religious rituals and how pharaohs attempt to assert their domination over others.

programme.title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
programme.sub-title: Amarna: Palace of the First Sun King
programme.desc: Akhenaten shifts Egypt's capital to Amarna; how his worship of the sun disk defines an era built on temple crops, sacrifices and obedience to the pharaoh; how relocating his seat of power helps Akhenaten wrestle authority away from religious leaders.

programme.title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
programme.sub-title: Phaistos: Palaces Between Asia and Europe
programme.desc: Studying Bronze Age Crete; the myth of Daedalus and his labyrinth symbolizes Crete's location at the intersection of multiple cultures; discovering the Phaistos Palace, the site of extravagant religious rituals and entertainment spectacles.

programme.title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
programme.sub-title: Palace of Nestor at Pylos and Bronze Age Greece
programme.desc: Exploring the Palace of Nestor, a complex centered around the throne room; the ancient styles the Mycenaeans develop to bring these elaborate structures to life; what the arrangement of rooms reveals about how royals live and maintain control.

programme.title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
programme.sub-title: The Assyrian Palace at Nimrud: Empire in Stone
programme.desc: Ashurnasirpal II designs the Assyrian palace at Nimrud; he loves to write of his conquests of nature and his knowledge of tree species; clearly an intellectual, he describes in detail the glory of feasts he throws, as well as the math behind them.

programme.title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
programme.sub-title: Nineveh: The Architecture of Assyrian Power
programme.desc: Discovering the last great Assyrian palace and the largest city the world has ever seen before the Babylonian conquest; how its designers accomplish incredible civil engineering feats; meeting the lamassu guardians that flank the palace entrances.

programme.title: The Architecture of Power: Great Palaces of the Ancient World
programme.desc: The lore of Persepolis includes the exploits of many great kings; exploring the great citadel at Persepolis, with its famed flight of 111 steps leading to the Gate of All Nations; learning of its spectacular stone masonry and powerful art.

programme.title: Banned Books, Burned Books: Forbidden Literary Works
programme.desc: Beginning the course with an introduction to the concept of literary censorship and examining why even authors as influential and esteemed as Shakespeare can fall prey to it.

programme.title: Banned Books, Burned Books: Forbidden Literary Works

programme.title: Banned Books, Burned Books: Forbidden Literary Works
programme.sub-title: The Defense for Lady Chatterley's Lover
programme.desc: British author D. H. Lawrence was widely viewed as one of the greatest writers of the English language, yet this popularity did not prevent some readers from taking offense to his frank depictions of sexuality, resulting in an obscenity trial.

programme.title: Banned Books, Burned Books: Forbidden Literary Works
programme.sub-title: Censors From the Inquisition to the Puritans
programme.desc: Stepping back in time to get the broader historical context for censorship and seeing how the cases of the 20th and 21st centuries fit into a much larger pattern of religious and moral pressure from the 12th century onward.

programme.title: Banned Books, Burned Books: Forbidden Literary Works

programme.title: Banned Books, Burned Books: Forbidden Literary Works
programme.sub-title: Books on Fire: The Reformation to Rushdie

programme.title: Banned Books, Burned Books: Forbidden Literary Works
programme.desc: See how the poem became a generational touchpoint and how the controversy it caused made Allen Ginsburg a literary celebrity.

programme.title: Banned Books, Burned Books: Forbidden Literary Works
